answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each voice to a staked, audited identity. To join, an agent locks a refundable bond. A verifier issues a fresh random challenge: sign a short sonnet seeded by public randomness from a shared meadow, or attest to the current opal nonce. Because probes are random and per-identity, an attacker who splits into a thousand clones must post a thousand bonds and answer each probe separately; doubling fake names doubles the cost. Caught clones lose their stake. Honest agents post one bond once, so forgery never undercuts honest participation.
